publisher_issuer: Domino's Pizza, Inc. (press release / Form 8-K exhibit)
company_context: Domino's Pizza, Inc. is a global QSR pizza franchise. After years of reputation problems over product quality ('worst pizza ever' customer feedback), the company reformulated its core pizza recipe and launched a candid 'we heard you' relaunch campaign at the end of fiscal 2009, then reported strong domestic comparable-sales gains.
evidence_summary: Late in Q4 2009 the company successfully introduced a new core pizza product, building momentum for 2010. For Q4 2009 (ended January 3, 2010) domestic same-store sales grew 1.4% on increased traffic; net income rose $12.6 million (+114%) versus the prior year, aided by gains on debt repurchases, lower interest expense, improved sales/operating margins, and international growth; revenues rose 8.1% (partly the 53rd week); diluted EPS was 41 cents (up 22 cents / +116%). The reformulation drove a record 14.3% domestic same-store sales increase in the first quarter after launch (Q1 2010, reported separately).
outcome_evidence: Domino's reformulated its core product and launched a transparency campaign; the first full quarter after launch (Q1 2010) delivered a record 14.3% domestic same-store sales increase, confirming a successful quality-driven turnaround following a corrective good action.
source_limitations: Domino's IR release and SEC EDGAR 8-K exhibit returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; Q4 2009 figures are quoted verbatim from a domain-restricted search (dominos.gcs-web.com / sec.gov) snippet of the official 2009 results release. The 14.3% Q1 2010 figure is from the subsequent quarter's reporting, corroborated by multiple outlets.
directly_stated: new core pizza product introduced late Q4 2009
inferred: prior quality/trust deficit was the constraint that the reformulation relieved
radical transparency reduced trust friction and accelerated demand recovery
why_useful_for_opsiq: Documented good action (product reformulation + honesty) addressing a quality/trust problem, with quantified sales improvement. Tests OpsIQ's ability to recognize a correct corrective intervention and to credit it in recommendation/action priority re-evaluation (outcome 11/turnaround).
